text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Arsenal and Burnley at the Emirates Stadium!

Arsenal's unbeaten start in the Premier League came to an end in a controversial manner last weekend as they were beaten 1-0 by Newcastle United, with Mikel Arteta blasting VAR's decision to let the winning goal stand in that game.
That was just days after they were knocked out of the EFL Cup by West Ham following a 3-1 defeat.
The Gunners have put that week behind them though, responding in the best fashion with a 2-0 win over Sevilla in the Champions League that puts them on the cusp of qualification.
Another win here would keep them in the mix at the top of the table.
Burnley couldn't be having a more different season.
They sit at the opposite end of the table in the relegation zone, with just four points to their name.
They've won just one game in the league this season (D1 L9), though that victory did come away from home as they beat Luton Town.
They've lost their last five on the bounce in all competitions, something they'll want to end quickly.
They have a good record against Arsenal though, losing just one of their last five against them in the competition (W1 D3).
Arteta makes just one change from the win over Sevilla in the Champions League in midweek, and it's an enforced one.
Ben White isn't in the squad, so Zinchenko comes in for him, with Tomiyasu switching out to the right.
Saka is able to start despite going off with an ankle injury in that game, while Nketiah is fit enough for the bench.
Kompany sticks with the same starting line-up that lost to Crystal Palace last weekend as he looks for a reaction today.
They are boosted by the return of Cullen from suspension, and Obafemi and Ramsey from injury, with all three of them named on the bench.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Amdouni gets the game under way for Burnley!
Arsenal are enjoying all of the early possession here, comfortably knocking it around between their defenders.
Burnley have barely ventured out of their own half, sitting deep to block off the space.
Saka does brilliantly to shake off Koleosho down the right, only to run into Taylor.
He's forced to go backwards, and Arsenal patiently start to mount another attack.
The hosts win the first corner of the game, and it's swung into the six-yard box by Saka.
Gabriel makes a late, unmarked run to the near post and gets his head to it, but he thumps it over the bar.
GOOD SAVE! Beyer's pass into Brownhill doesn't quite some off as referee Michael Oliver gets in the way, but Amdouni keeps it alive as he runs onto the loose ball.
He takes it to the edge of the box before having a shot, and Raya dives to tip it wide.
Arsenal lost and failed to score for the first time in the Premier League this season last time out against Newcastle, managing just one shot on target all game.
However, they're unbeaten in their last 37 home league games against promoted sides (W32 D5).
After a slightly slow start to the game, Burnley are starting to get a slight foothold here.
They're keeping the ball well in their own half, though Arsenal's high press is causing some issues when they try to move it forward.
Trossard gets his first real chance to run at Burnley's defence here and slides it through to Martinelli when he makes the overlapping run.
O'Shea spots the danger early though and is able to stop a cross from coming in.
It doesn't look like Saliba has many options available, but then he gets his head up to spot Rice darting into the box.
He lofts a long ball over the top, but Trafford is quickly off his line to pluck it out of the air ahead of the midfielder.
Arsenal's patient play isn't getting them anywhere, so Tomiyasu goes for the big switch out to Martinelli.
He cushions it into Zinchenko, who loops a cross to the far post, but Havertz's corner is deflected wide.
GREAT SAVE! Burnley just can't clear their lines here! Saka cuts inside from the right, only to see his throughball blocked.
It pinballs off the Clarets defenders, and Saka takes his chance, firing it at the near top corner.
Trafford stretches to tip it onto the bar.
It's lovely play from Burnley as they knock it upfield, and Gudmundsson has space to run down the right.
He tries to square it to Rodriguez on the edge of the box, but Gabriel steps in to cut it out.
Arsenal are asking for a penalty here after Saka goes down in the box.
It was actually a wonderful tackle from O'Shea, who raced back into possession to stop Saka from finishing off a quick counter.
It's a lovely bit of skill from Zinchenko, who draws three defenders in before flicking it back to Saka on the right.
He squares it into the middle, and Trossard just misses it, before Havertz's first-time volley is blocked by Beyer's outstretched leg.
GOOD SAVE! Arsenal are upping the pressure here and Saka nods the ball towards goal.
The final touch comes off Beyer, whose header loops towards his own goal, and Trafford scrambles back to claw it off the line.
The possession stats are just starting to lean in Arsenal's favour as the hosts keep Burnley penned back in their own half.
The wingers are starting to get a bit more space, with Martinelli swinging in a cross, but Beyer clears it.
CHANCE! Arsenal win their fifth corner here and Saka swings another dangerous cross into the crowded six-yard box.
Havertz meets it this time, but gets caught under it, heading his effort over the bar.
GOOD SAVE! Raya is tested once more after Arsenal are caught out by a long ball.
A loose touch from Saliba plays Gudmundsson through the middle and he sends it across goal, but Raya gets a strong hand to it.
SAVE! Arsenal may be showing their dominance, but Burnley have tested Raya will all four of their shots so far.
The space just opens up for Rodriguez as he cuts inside from the left, so he tries his luck from range.
The keeper holds onto this one.
Arsenal win another corner, but Martinelli sees it cleared at the near post.
The Gunners manage to keep it alive on the far side through Saka, but then Trossard drags a low cross behind everybody still inside the box.
GREAT SAVE! So many times this season, Burnley have lost the ball deep in their own half before conceding, and it almost happens again.
Brownhill gives it away and it's worked to Trossard, who takes aim from the edge of the box, but Trafford gets a strong hand behind the shot.
Burnley almost turn the tables here as Martinelli is chased back towards his own goal with the ball.
Zinchenko miscontrolled the pass, not realising that Amdouni is hovering on the edge of the box, but Jorginho just gets there first.
Kompany is shaking his head on the touchline once more as O'Shea gives the ball away on the edge of his own box.
Luckily, it ricochets off Trossard and Vitinho does well to win a throw-in and ease the pressure.
Koleosho isn't happy with the referee as he doesn't get a free-kick in his favour.
He's ready to make a darting run into the box so he can be picked out by Rodriguez, but he has his heels clipped by Saka before he can get going.
Two Burnley players try to trip Martinelli, but he stays on his feet to keep the move alive.
He cuts back from the byline only to loop a too deep cross into the box which misses everybody.
TROSSARD SCORES! Just before half-time, Arsenal finally break Burnley down! Zinchenko has put some good crosses into the box, and this is no different as he picks out Saka.
He cushions a header back towards the near post and Trossard is brave as he throws himself onto the end of it.
He nods it past Trafford before colliding with the post.
1-0 Arsenal!
It's a good run from Saka to the edge of the six-yard box, and he gets us behind Beyer to nod it back into the danger area.
Trossard stays down holding his shoulder after that heavy collision with the post.
It initially looks bad as the medical team rush on, but the Belgian is able to move his arm, which means he'll be coming back on.
HALF-TIME: ARSENAL 1-0 BURNLEY.
Trossard leaves it late to break the deadlock as Arsenal take a 1-0 lead over Burnley into half-time.

The Gunners were the dominant side in the first half, but they struggled to break down a compact Clarets side for the most part - Trafford was forced into a couple of good saves to deny Saka and Martinelli.
He was beaten in the 46th minute though as Trossard rushed forward to head in from very close range.
Burnley have shown a threat at the other end though, with Raya making four saves to keep them out.
Arteta will be pleased with what he's seen so far, especially after such a poor performance last time out in the Premier League.
Their patience paid off, and he'll be looking for them to build on this, hopefully with Trossard still leading the attack after his injury.
There are positives for Burnley despite being behind, and Kompany will be urging them to still take risks to get back into this game.
Arsenal get us back under way for the second half!
Burnley are straight out of the traps here as Koleosho bursts down the left, leaving defenders in his wake.
Raya rushes off his line, but the winger takes it around him before winning a corner.
It comes to nothing though.
Despite that heavy collision with the post just before the break, Trossard is back out for the second half, still leading the line.
His goal was actually Arsenal's 1000th goal at the Emirates Stadium in all competitions.
It's lovely play down Arsenal's left as Martinelli plays a one-two with Zinchenko.
The Brazilian clips it into the middle where Gabriel is waiting, but the defender goes down softly after a nudge from Rodriguez.
He gets nothing from the referee.
This is a good spell for Burnley and they're keeping Arsenal penned back in their own half.
Koleosho is still causing problems down the left, and the Gunners can't get out.
BROWNHILL EQUALISES! It's all about Koleosho's run to start the move, and it looks like Tomiyasu has it covered, but the defender is just outmuscled as he goes to ground.
Koleosho keeps it alive, pulling it back to Rodriguez, but he's closed down by Gabriel.
The deflection falls to Brownhill, with a deflection off Rodriguez taking it past Raya.
The goal passes a quick VAR check, and it's 1-1!
GOOD SAVE! Arsenal want a quick response to that equaliser and the pace of their attack is more than Burnley can handle.
Martinelli has space down the left, and Trafford rushes out to block his low shot when he cuts into the box.
SALIBA SCORES! Burnley weren't level for long! Trossard goes over to take the corner and he whips a cross right onto the goal line.
Trafford gets blocked in and is beaten to the ball by Saliba, who nods in from close range.
2-1 Arsenal!
It's a brilliant corner from Trossard who curled his delivery right on top of Trafford, who couldn't get the better of Saliba.
Arsenal were ready to make this change before they retook the lead, but they now have the chance to do it.
Havertz goes off, with Vieira on in his place.
Burnley are back to being pegged back deep in their own half, and it was their goal that breathed some life back into Arsenal.
Martinelli has space down the left once more but has no one in the box in support.
Trossard whips another dangerous corner across the face of goal and it's just glanced away from Gabriel by Berge.
Nobody is running onto it at the far post for Arsenal, and Taylor hooks it away.
A neat bit of footwork from Amdouni gets him away from Jorginho and he's able to switch it out to Gudmundsson who gets Burnley over the halfway line.
It's worked out to Koleosho on the far side, but he blasts his shot high and wide.
CLOSE! Trossard just overruns the ball as he tries to get into space on the edge of the box, but O'Shea's interception actually sits up nicely for Rice.
He races onto it, hitting the strike first time, but it curls inches wide of the far post.
Arsenal's corner count continues to go up as Trossard makes his way over once more.
This corner isn't as close to the goal line, but it still gets stuck into the ground until Berge puts his laces through a clearance.
Arteta has never managed to beat Burnley, drawing one and losing one of his previous meetings with the Clarets when they were managed by Sean Dyche.
His team are on the attack again to try and make sure of three points here.
Martinelli is causing all sorts of problems down the left, and Vitinho is struggling to keep up with him.
His cross is blocked, with Arsenal now up to their 12th corner in this game, and it's Trossard to whip it in again.
WHAT A GOAL! It's incredible by Zinchenko! Trossard whips the corner into the box, and it hits O'Shea, who watches with relief as it smacks the crossbar.
The rebound bounces in front of Zinchenko, who leaps up to volley it, almost karate kick style, past a static Trafford and into the far top corner.
3-1 Arsenal!
Kompany is readying some changes as he aims to try and get a second goal here, but this game looks like it's probably beyond Burnley.
Arsenal are keeping comfortable possession, giving them no way out of their own half.
Vitinho gets in a bit of a tangle trying to hold off Martinelli and ends up prodding it out for yet another Arsenal corner.
Trafford pushes Trossard's latest delivery away, but Burnley's respite is short.
It's a double change for Burnley here.
Bruun Larsen, who scored the winning goal against Luton in the Clarets' only victory this season, is brought on for Koleosho.
And Ramsey is given a run-out after shaking off a knock.
He replaces Amdoni.
There's a double change for Arsenal now.
The scorer of the opening goal, Trossard, is replaced by Nketiah, who scored a hat-trick in his last appearance at the Emirates.
And Saka is also making way, with Nelson on in his place.
VIEIRA IS SENT OFF! Taylor nods the ball down to Brownhill, who is the favourite to get to it.
Vieira sticks a leg out almost lazily, and he catches the Burnley midfielder high on the shin.
The collision looked accidental, but it's a really poor challenge and he's given his marching orders.
Arsenal will finish the game with 10 men.
Obafemi has had a lot of injury problems so far this season, but he's getting a chance to come on here.
He replaces the goalscorer, Brownhill.
Burnley win just their third corner of the game and O'Shea makes a darting run to the near post to get on the end of it.
His header loops up into the air, and doesn't trouble Raya as it lands on the roof of the net.
Burnley's final roll of the dice sees Odobert come on for Vitinho.
Martinelli goes down holding his hamstring, and after receiving some treatment, he's going to go off.
Arteta is using the opportunity to bring on an extra defender in Kiwior.
We're into six added minutes here with Burnley on the attack still.
The visitors have a bit more belief now due to their man advantage, but Arsenal are defending staunchly.
There's an off-the-ball incident between Gabriel and Rodriguez in the box.
The defender initially shoves Rodriguez out of the way, with the striker then throwing out an arm.
After a quick VAR check, we're okay to continue with nothing more found in it.
Gudmundsson is late getting across to Rice and just steps across him to stop the run.
He picks up the first yellow card of the game.
Burnley are still trying to push forward in search of another goal, but time is starting to run out here.
Berge slides a wonderful throughball into Bruun Larsen, but his pullback isn't near a team-mate.
As Arsenal defended that last Burnley attack, Jorginho went down holding his head.
He was actually caught by Kiwior, who was trying to flick the ball away, and the Italian requires treatment.
Jorginho is back on his feet, but the cut on his head is still bleeding.
He's going to be taken off so that he can be patched up and Arsenal will be able to make a concussion substitution if there's time.
FULL-TIME: ARSENAL 3-1 BURNLEY.
Arsenal are back to winning ways in the Premier League with a 3-1 victory over Burnley.
It took the Gunners a long time to break their opponents down, with Trossard nodding them in front from close range just before half-time.
Burnley fought back in the second half as Brownhill equalised, with a bit of help from Rodriguez, as his deflected shot wrong-footed Raya.
They weren't level for long though, with Saliba getting the better of Trafford to head in a corner on the line before Zinchenko scored a spectacular acrobatic volley to secure the three points.
Arsenal had to finish the game with 10 men after Vieira was sent off for a late, high challenge on Brownhill, but they were able to comfortably see it out.
They're level on points at the top of the table with Manchester City, who don't play until tomorrow, and they travel to Brentford after the international break.
Burnley's miserable run continues as they stay 19th, and it's West Ham at home up next for them.
That's all for today, goodbye!
